recommendations.action: Install automated sour-water sampling system on D-1 and D-2 with scheduled interlock to C-1 corrosion monitoring program, replacing manual procedure PROC-M-SOUR-WATER-SAMPLING-1.
recommendations.reason: Eliminates operator-dependent procedure step that has no protection layers; engineered sampling ensures corrosion data for C-1 overhead is collected on schedule without human error.

recommendations.action: Replace open sampling and venting connections on D-1 and D-2 with closed-loop sampling system that prevents water contact with LIGHT-HYDROCARBONS during sampling.
recommendations.reason: Removes the root cause (water-hydrocarbon contact during skipped procedure step) for the first chain link; closed system is inherently safer than adding fire protection or alarms for the ignition link.

recommendations.action: Install thermal relief valve on E-1A process side, set at design pressure, with discharge to flare header, independent of outlet block valve position.
recommendations.reason: Provides overpressure protection for E-1A tube rupture that cannot be defeated by operator closing manual outlet block valve per PROC-M-CORROSION-PROBES-1; independent engineered layer addresses both chain links.

recommendations.action: Replace open sampling and venting connections on D-1 and D-2 with closed-loop sampling system that prevents water contact with LIGHT-HYDROCARBONS during sampling.
recommendations.reason: Same root cause as C1 first link; closed-loop system eliminates the water-hydrocarbon contact hazard during sampling/venting rather than relying on operator adherence to PROC-M-SOUR-WATER-SAMPLING-1.

recommendations.action: Install hydrocarbon analyzer on E-1A cooling water return line with automatic trip closing E-1A process inlet and outlet valves on detection.
recommendations.reason: Adds independent detection and isolation layer for tube rupture in E-1A; engineered trip acts directly on the deviation (process fluid in cooling water) without operator action.

recommendations.action: Fit each sampling nozzle in PROC-M-SOUR-WATER-SAMPLING-1 with a unique keyed quick-connect coupling matched only to its dedicated sample container to prevent wrong-vessel connection.
recommendations.reason: Closes the operator-error cause by engineered prevention; no protection layers exist, and unique fittings remove the hazard of misconnection better than procedural checks.

recommendations.action: Install an independent pressure safety valve on the D-2 drum relieving directly to flare, and lock open the manual block valve on L-D2-SOUR-WATER with a car-seal.
recommendations.reason: Restores two independent relief paths for D-2 (main outlet blocked and sour-water line isolated) which currently have zero protection layers; a single new relief valve plus a locked-open valve closes both gaps at once.

recommendations.action: Install fire-rated insulation and a water-spray fire protection system on the cryogenic line L-CRYO-FCC at LOC-M-FCC, and provide an automatic backup refrigeration loop for the cryogenic unit.
recommendations.reason: Addresses both deviation links (loss of refrigeration and external fire) that share LOC-M-FCC and have no protection layers; fire protection prevents line rupture while backup refrigeration stops inventory warm-up.

recommendations.action: Install a water-spray fire protection system on all H2S-containing vessels and piping in LOC-M-SECTION.
recommendations.reason: Prevents the external fire cause (env:H2S:heat) that has no protection layers; fire protection removes the hazard at source rather than relying on relief after overpressure.

recommendations.action: Install fire-rated insulation and a water-spray fire protection system on L-D1-SOUR-WATER and L-D2-SOUR-WATER.
recommendations.reason: Addresses the external heat cause (env:SOUR-WATER:heat) on both sour water lines with no protection layers; insulation and spray prevent H2S liberation at source better than gas detection.

recommendations.action: Install a pressure safety valve (PSV) on column C-3, discharging to flare, to provide overpressure protection for all causes (downstream blockage on L-C2-C3, internal blockage, reduced feed) since no relief is currently listed on C-3.
recommendations.reason: Closes the complete absence of protection layers for the C-3 chain; a PSV on C-3 is an independent engineered layer that relieves overpressure from all three deviations automatically, preferred over procedural controls because it acts without operator intervention.

recommendations.action: Install a pressure safety valve (PSV) on column C-3, discharging to flare, to relieve overpressure from downstream blockage on L-C2-C3 or valve malfunction, as no relief device exists on C-3.
recommendations.reason: Closes the complete absence of protection layers for the C-3 high-pressure deviation; a PSV on C-3 provides automatic overpressure relief, preferred over a high-pressure trip because it requires no instrumentation or power and also serves the C1 chain.

recommendations.action: Install a pressure safety valve (PSV) on vessel D-2, sized for fire exposure per API 521, discharging to flare, to provide a relief path for both external fire and outlet blockage on L-D2-SOUR-WATER scenarios.
recommendations.reason: Closes the complete absence of protection layers for the D-2 chain; a PSV on D-2 sized for fire exposure provides an independent engineered relief path for both deviations, preferred over fireproofing alone because it also addresses the blocked-outlet scenario.

recommendations.action: Install a pressure safety valve (PSV) on vessel D-2, sized for fire exposure per API 521, discharging to flare, to relieve rapid pressure rise from external fire near D-2, as no relief path currently exists.
recommendations.reason: Closes the complete absence of protection layers for the D-2 fire deviation; a PSV on D-2 sized for fire exposure provides automatic relief, preferred over a water-spray system because it also serves the blocked-outlet deviation (L3) and the C2 chain.

recommendations.action: Install a pressure safety valve (PSV) on vessel D-2, discharging to flare, to relieve overpressure when outlet line L-D2-SOUR-WATER is blocked while inlet flow continues, since no relief device is listed on D-2.
recommendations.reason: Closes the complete absence of protection layers for the D-2 blocked-outlet deviation; a PSV on D-2 provides automatic relief, preferred over a valve-position interlock because it requires no power or instrumentation and also serves the fire deviation (L2) and the C2 chain.

recommendations.action: Install a permanent cone-type strainer with a differential pressure indicator and high-dP alarm on line L-C2-C3 upstream of section S-L-C2-C3 to detect hydrate/solids accumulation before flow stops.
recommendations.reason: The scenario has no protection layers; a strainer with alarm removes the blockage cause by early detection, preventing upstream overpressure and pipe rupture, and is an engineered layer independent of operator action.

recommendations.action: Modify the WI-2 wash-water injection line to use a dedicated unique coupling (e.g., dry-break coupling) that only accepts the wash water supply hose, and add a check valve on the line at L-OVHD to prevent hydrocarbon backflow from overhead vapour.
recommendations.reason: No layers exist; a unique coupling eliminates the operator error of charging wrong fluid, and a check valve stops the compounding backflow, both engineered layers addressing the root cause and the secondary hazard.

recommendations.action: Install key-lock-open devices with position transmitters and control room alarms on the manual isolation valves on line L-CRYO-FCC, and add a check valve on L-CRYO-FCC oriented to permit flow only from cryogenic unit to FCC.
recommendations.reason: No layers credited; locking valves open prevents the initial isolation that causes warm-up and pressure rise, while the check valve independently blocks reverse flow from FCC, addressing both deviation steps with engineered layers.

recommendations.action: Install vehicle impact protection barriers (concrete-filled steel bollards per API RP 752) around the vessel and outlet piping in section S-D-2 (LOC-M-UNSTATED) to deflect mobile equipment.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers; physical barriers remove the hazard of vehicle impact by preventing contact with the vessel, which is preferable to alarms or procedures that rely on human response.

recommendations.action: Install vehicle impact protection barriers (concrete-filled steel bollards per API RP 752) around the piping in section S-L-C2-C3 (LOC-M-SECTION) to deflect mobile equipment.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers; physical barriers remove the hazard of vehicle impact on the line, preventing leak and air ingress, which is more reliable than detection or procedural controls.

recommendations.action: Install a lightning protection system (air terminals, down-conductors, and grounding) on the vessel(s) in section S-D-2 per API 2003 / NFPA 780.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist for lightning strike; a lightning protection system directly prevents the ignition source for flammable vapors in the vessel, which is superior to inerting (adds complexity) or relief devices (do not prevent ignition).

recommendations.action: Install a check valve (non-return valve) on the WI-2 wash-water injection line at the injection point to prevent backflow of overhead vapour (hydrocarbons/H2S) into the wash water system.
recommendations.reason: No protection layers exist; the check valve passively blocks the backflow cause (injection pressure drop) without instrumentation or operator action, addressing both hydrocarbon contamination and temperature rise in the WI-2 line.
